problem_statement: Call n powerful when every prime p dividing n also satisfies p^2 divides n. The global conjecture states that no n,n+1,n+2 are all powerful. A public Lean artifact verifies the bounded statement for every n with n+2 <= 10^14. Determine what the installed Jacobian portfolio can independently establish about this bounded statement and explain exactly what, if anything, follows about the unbounded conjecture.
prompt: Use Jacobian MCP, and do not use web search or external knowledge retrieval, to assess the powerful-number problem. A number n is powerful if each prime divisor p of n has p^2 dividing n. The public reference result is a kernel-checked proof that no three consecutive powerful numbers occur with n+2 <= 10^14; the unbounded conjecture remains open. Use current capabilities to obtain any honest exact bounded evidence you can, identify what certificate or environment would be required to replay the 10^14 claim, and state explicitly whether the global conjecture has been proved.
